body:
## Summary
The candidate education level 'university' means 'the CV names a school but states no degree', yet the matcher ranks it below 'bachelor' and hard-knocks the candidate out of every bachelor/master/PhD role - while a CV that names no school at all ('unknown') is explicitly not penalized. Give education one module (`pipeline/jobfit/education.py`) that owns both ladders and a three-valued gate (meets / below / uncertain), make 'degree unstated' uncertain, and derive every hand-copied list from it.

## Description
Education is the one KO in ko_filter whose input is not a fact but an inference from a surface match. Today its vocabulary lives in seven hand-copied lists with two different memberships (job side: none/high_school/university/bachelor/master/phd; candidate side: unknown/university/bachelor/master/phd), and the rank that joins them (`_EDU_RANK`, matching.py:45) silently equates the candidate's 'attended, degree unstated' with the job's 'any university degree'. The consequence is a fairness inversion: an English CV that writes 'Charles University, 2012-2017' is knocked out of a bachelor role; the same CV written in Czech ('Univerzita Karlova') classifies as unknown and passes. The structural move is one module that states which pairs are measurable: `education_gate(candidate_level, job_min) -> 'not_required' | 'meets' | 'below' | 'uncertain'`. ko_filter knocks out only on 'below'; 'uncertain' widens the confidence band with a new driver/assumption code `eduDegreeUnstated` (the same honesty the 'unknown' branch already gives). jobs.py, taxonomy.py, transform.py, profile_draft_cli.py and pipeline.py import the tuples instead of re-typing them; codegen emits CANDIDATE_EDUCATION_LEVELS so profileTypes.ts stops hand-listing the editor's options. winnability, recruiter rows, matrix cells and the match meta all read ko_filter, so they follow without edits.

## Flow
1. Add `pipeline/jobfit/education.py`: JOB_MIN_LEVELS, CANDIDATE_LEVELS, the ordinal ranks, CLASSIFY_PRIORITY, FOUNDATION weights, `education_gate`.
2. Switch jobs.py:47, taxonomy.py:977, transform.py:57, profile_draft_cli.py:46, pipeline.py:663-666 to import them (behaviour-neutral commit; the identity test lands first).
3. matching.py: ko_filter's education branch calls `education_gate` and appends a KoReason only on 'below'; `_confidence` and `_candidate_assumption_pairs` add `eduDegreeUnstated` for level 'university'.
4. Catalogs: match.drivers.eduDegreeUnstated + match.assumptions.eduDegreeUnstated in en/cs/de/fr.
5. codegen.py render_taxonomy emits CANDIDATE_EDUCATION_LEVELS; profileTypes.ts:130 re-exports it as EDU_LEVELS; regenerate taxonomy.generated.ts.
6. docs/features/matching/README.md: the KO table states the three-valued gate and why 'degree unstated' is uncertain.

## Expected impact
Every candidate whose CV names a school without a degree title stops being silently removed from bachelor+ roles on the candidate->jobs match, the recruiter ranking, the fit matrix and winnability; the recruiter sees an honest 'degree not stated' band driver instead. The education vocabulary drops from seven copies to one, so the next level added (e.g. a VOŠ diploma) is a one-line change the codegen check carries to TS. Measured shortfalls (high_school vs bachelor) still knock out, so no real floor is loosened.

## Evaluation
Claim: 'degree unstated' is uncertain, never a KO; measured shortfalls still KO; the vocabulary has one source.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7

body:
## Summary
On the job-seeker feed a posting the hard filter removed is indistinguishable from one the scan has not reached: both say 'Not scored', the detail page literally says 'did not pass the hard filters, or the scan has not matched it yet', and the matcher re-spends on every filtered posting on every scan. Return the blocked postings from the engine with their gate and an as-if score, stamp them so the incremental scan skips them, and let the feed say 'Filtered: work mode' with 'would score 78' behind it.

## Description
The seeker's own preferences (workModes, seniority) and the profile's languages drive ko_filter, and match() discards every job that fails it, keeping only a count. The eligibility chips were built to show exactly these axes, but they are computed only on survivors, so the three KO-mirrored chips can never light up on /me. The seeker therefore cannot see that their 'remote only' setting is hiding a 78-point onsite role in their own city - a decision made blind with data the engine already computed. The leap: an opt-in `include_blocked` on match() returns, per filtered job, the KO keys, the details and the full MatchResult scored as if the gate were lifted (score_job is already gate-independent; the recruiter ranking calls it on KO'd candidates today). The seeker scan stores that verdict in match_json with match_total NULL - so sorting, the deep-dive shortlist and the fit tier stay exactly as honest as now - and stamps match_version so the row is not re-matched until the profile or posting changes. The UI turns the dead 'Not scored' into a named, actionable state: the chip names the gate, the detail shows the as-if score and links to the preference that caused it.

## Flow
1. matching.py: `BlockedMatch{job_id, ko_keys, ko_details, result}`; `MatchResponse.blocked` (default empty, excluded from the dump when empty); `match(..., include_blocked=False)` scores KO'd jobs only when asked.
2. match_cli.py: `--include-blocked`; correct the --preferences-json help.
3. match.ts: pass the flag, parse `blocked` into `outcome.blocked`, filter koKeys to the KoReasonKey vocabulary; bump MATCH_VERSION to jobseeker-match-v2.
4. jobseeker-postings.ts: `setPostingBlocked` (re-check on job_json IS NOT NULL); projectMatch reads `blocked.koKeys` into `blockedBy`.
5. scan.ts: stamp each blocked row after the matched rows; keep the ko_filtered log line.
6. types.ts: KoReasonKey + `blockedBy` on JobseekerPostingSummary.
7. postingView.ts: `blocked` view beside `match`; PostingRow / PostingDetail / FitSheet render it; catalogs x4; both docs.

## Expected impact
Every filtered posting on /me stops being a mystery: the seeker sees which of their own settings removed it and what it would have scored, and can widen the setting knowingly instead of never learning the role existed. Re-scans stop re-matching the filtered tail (a remote-only seeker over a mostly-onsite dataset re-sent most of the dataset every scan). The engine's promise that eligibility shows 'every axis uniformly' becomes true for the first time.

## Evaluation
Claim: a filtered posting is stored once with its gate and as-if score, shown as such on every seeker surface, and skipped by the next unchanged scan.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: contract
Result: pending build
Gate: contract
